Family.basisOfRecord_reasoning: The study relies on field observations of live organisms (moths) in their natural habitat (riparian forests) using automated light traps. The measurements involve ecological traits and community structure derived from these in situ observations, fitting the definition of HumanObservation for ecological/behavioral traits.
Family.measurementMethod: Moths were collected using automated light traps (15 W tubes) placed 1 m above ground under a closed forest canopy, run for approximately 6 hours at dusk, once a month over two annual cycles (2006–2008). Ecological traits were assembled for 448 species from faunal monographs and databases. Phylogenetic trees were reconstructed using COI barcodes obtained from the Barcode of Life Datasystems (BOLD) and analyzed using RAxML and BEAST.
Family.measurementMethod_reasoning: The methodology describes the specific protocols used for data collection (light-trapping parameters), trait data acquisition (assembly from literature/databases), and phylogenetic analysis (COI barcoding and Bayesian tree reconstruction).

Subfamily.basisOfRecord_reasoning: The data (species counts, functional traits, and phylogenetic information) were derived from moths collected and identified using automated light traps at 28 field sites. The specimens were physically collected and subsequently analyzed for traits and DNA sequences.
Subfamily.measurementMethod: Moths were collected using automated light traps (15 W tubes) at 28 sites in lowland forest stands along three rivers in easternmost Austria (2006–2008). Species were identified to species level. Functional traits (27 traits) were assembled from literature and databases. Phylogenetic trees were reconstructed using COI barcode sequences obtained from BOLD. Diversity metrics (SD, FD, PD) and community-weighted means (CWMs) were calculated using specific R packages (SpadeR, FD, pez, picante) and analyzed using two-way ANOVAs.
